flashcard_questions.q: What is a high-level programming language?
flashcard_questions.a: A language written with English-like keywords that must be translated before it runs.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is high-level code described as portable?
flashcard_questions.a: The same program can run on different types of computer once translated.

flashcard_questions.q: What is machine code in a computer?
flashcard_questions.a: Pure binary instructions the processor runs directly, with no translation needed.

flashcard_questions.q: What does assembly language use in place of binary?
Why is low-level code described as machine-specific?
flashcard_questions.a: It only works on one type of processor.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the main benefit of writing in a low-level language?
flashcard_questions.a: It runs very fast and uses little memory.

flashcard_questions.q: What is source code in programming?
flashcard_questions.a: The code a programmer writes before it is translated into machine code.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a compiler translate a program?
flashcard_questions.a: It translates the whole program in one go, before it is run.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a compiler produce from source code?
flashcard_questions.a: A separate executable file of machine code.

flashcard_questions.q: When does a compiler report the mistakes it has found?
flashcard_questions.a: At the end, as one error report listing them together.

flashcard_questions.q: How does an interpreter translate a program?
flashcard_questions.a: One statement at a time, as the program runs.

flashcard_questions.q: What does an interpreter do when it meets the first error?
flashcard_questions.a: It stops and reports that error straight away.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does an interpreted program run more slowly?
flashcard_questions.a: The interpreter translates as it goes, every time the program runs.

flashcard_questions.q: What is an Integrated Development Environment?
flashcard_questions.a: A single application bringing together the tools needed to write, run and debug programs.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a breakpoint do in an IDE?
flashcard_questions.a: It pauses the running program at a chosen line.

notes: 15 cards: 6 term-to-definition, 5 translator-behaviour, 4 causal. Compiler and interpreter cards each name the translator in the front so the pair cannot interfere. Dropped the syntax-highlighting IDE card to stay at 15.
